docs.text: "Given that the Great Lakes — and their aquatic life — straddle both sides of the border, having American scientists suddenly barred from meetings has had deep impacts." www.cbc.ca/news/science...

As Rémi Quirion said in this article, "Science should be without borders". This is especially true for shared ecosystems like the Great Lakes. To have so many important projects shut down, and for researchers to no longer be able to share important environmental knowledge is so alarming.

5/15 Cross-border research particularly hit: Great Lakes projects studying fish migration and climate impacts now on hold. "It's like the border doesn't exist," says Fisk of previous collaboration. #GreatLakes #Research

We were part of an NSF proposal for a five year study of the Great Lakes as a potential landing place for migration (among other research aspects in the proposal). It didn't go through, but that deep research should be going on everywhere now.

Scientists Barred from sharing
Canadian ecologist Aaron Fisk tried to set up a virtual call to discuss plans with American colleagues, around sampling fish. "We tried to have a quick meeting with one of our collaborators…and they were denied access," Fisk said. The Great Lakes straddle the border.

When anti-science meets erosion of freedom. “Given that the Great Lakes — and their aquatic life — straddle both sides of the border, having American scientists suddenly barred from meetings has had deep impacts.” www.cbc.ca/news/science...

4/ The Isolation Trap (§200.432 & §200.220): Conference attendance requires agency pre-approval. Cross-border partnerships face new hurdles. This isolates U.S. researchers from global networks essential for managing transboundary ecosystems like the Laurentian Great Lakes.

“Given that the Great Lakes — and their aquatic life — straddle both sides of the border, having American scientists suddenly barred from meetings has had deep impacts. That, combined with funding freezes, is drastically altering the way science works in North America, at least for now.”
So much for co-management of the Great Lakes. Maybe scientists can communicate on Signal. Actually, I hope they already are. Resist.
